doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Swing broadcasts heard as a boy
summary: Sneaking the radio to hear Woody Herman, Basie and Ellington late at night.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: But when you were let’s say ten years old, can you remember what you might have been hearing on the radio?

Oh the swing things. The big bands. I remember I used to listen and Woody Herman, he used to come from the Left Bank out of somewhere in New Jersey on a Saturday night after midnight. And I would have to go to bed and listen, because my parents, but we would sneak the radio in the room and I would have my head like on one of the things and listen to Woody Herman’s band coming from, what is it Left Bank? Because they had that club in New Jersey? I forgot. But I used to listen to Woody coming from the Left Bank at night. And at different other broadcasts at night, he used to bring Basie on every night and Duke Ellington on every night. I caught all of that.
